title: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes
summary: Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on. All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years". title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
summary: New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together. Read more

title: This week in PC games: start a new life in Vice City, escape a dying universe before the last black hole evaporates, and avenge your pigeon with a sledgehammer
summary: Happy this week, all! Please throw yourself upon the floor in consternation, clawing at your face and hair, for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6 is nigh. In just a few short days, every gaming vertical under the sun will be publishing features about the exact depth of Jason Duval's ripped abs and what this Says About America Today, or how many bottle caps you must gather to unlock Lucia Caminos' Gundam mode. Fortunately for my sanity, Rockstar's crime colossus isn't yet nigh on PC, though the word is that modders driven nuts by Claude will soon be along with an unofficial "port" . As such, while we do have a few Grandiosely Thievish articles in store this week – not least, coverage of the on-going unionisation situation at Rockstar – we can afford to spend a few hours writing about non-GTA things. The appraisal of mushrooms, for example, or the solubility of rubber hosing, or the parrying of spells. Without further ado, here's this week's uncommonly flavourful crop of new PC games. Don't worry, dear Maw. You'll get to eat Jason eventually. Read more

title: "We've finally reached this milestone": Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP kicks off open beta after around six years preparing for cybermayhem
summary: After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta". Read more
